source.title: Gradient descent fails to learn high-frequency functions and modular arithmetic
source.authors: Rustem Takhanov; Maxat Tezekbayev; Artur Pak; A. Bolatov; Z. Assylbekov

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses grokking and modular-arithmetic learning, but its results concern gradient-variance bounds and learning difficulty, not delayed generalization after training accuracy saturates or the other listed version-specific behaviors.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions reported grokking results from prior work, but those are not this study's results. Its own experiments and bounds concern high-frequency-wave and modular-arithmetic learning; they do not measure the overfitting-to-late-generalization trajectory in V1 or the other listed version-specific outcomes. Figure values not stated in the text are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The paper proves gradient-variance (barren plateau) bounds and SQ-dimension lower bounds for high-frequency waves and modular multiplication with a random secret multiplier, and runs small experiments showing failure to learn. It never tracks train vs test accuracy over time, so it cannot show delayed generalization. It does not vary training-set size, weight decay or initialization scale, and does not identify circuits. Grokking appears only in the introduction (cited prior work) and as an open problem in the conclusion. Its task (learning x→a·x mod p for unknown a) differs from the original grokking task (learning a binary operation table).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors show gradient concentration (variance about Õ(1/√p) or Õ(1/√A)), so gradient methods fail for large p or A, and they derive SQ-dimension lower bounds. Experiments suggest the variance decays faster, like 1/p. They leave the link to grokking (the Goldilocks zone, the LU mechanism) as an open problem.
record.recipe_differences: The study gives mathematical gradient-variance bounds and experiments on learning waves and modular arithmetic; it does not reproduce the original grokking training setup or measure the claimed delayed-generalization trajectory.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported learnability outcome varies with modular-multiplication bit length; all-bit accuracies also vary with bit position because the classes are unbalanced.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient variance over modular-multiplication and high-frequency-wave hypothesis classes shrinks as p or A grows. Empirically, small dense networks fail to learn these targets at larger bit lengths or frequencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning modular multiplication with an unknown multiplier (or high-frequency waves) by gradient descent faces a barren plateau. The gradient variance is bounded by Õ(1/√p), which implies failure at large p.

record.problems: The empirical learning outcomes are chiefly described in plots, and the text does not report numerical accuracy or MSE values for the modular-multiplication figures. The experiments do not isolate grokking dynamics or vary training-set size to test the claimed delay relationship. The theoretical results are bounds under stated assumptions, not direct demonstrations of training trajectories.
record.rows_left_out: No separate per-bitlength or per-bit numerical rows were extracted from Figures 3 and 6 because the text does not state those values; the reported text-level trends and longer-bitlength outcome are recorded in r2 and r3.

untested.parts: Never tests whether test accuracy jumps late after training accuracy saturates, or how the delay scales with training-set size. The experiments report only final or loss curves showing failure.
No progress measures and no circuit analysis.
No non-algorithmic data, and initialization scale and weight norm are not varied.
No weight decay, no critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
No test of optimizer or numerical artifacts.

missing.what: Empirical fit of mean squared covariance between a·X and b·X (about 0.015·p³·(log p)^0.42). This supports the approximate-orthogonality argument and bears on no version.

record.verdict_notes: Not a source of the claim. The record's T6/discusses classification is sound. The paper's own experiments use Adam on dense networks with a fixed random multiplier and do not exhibit or measure grokking.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test training accuracy saturation, test accuracy staying at chance and then rising late, or how that delay varies with training-set size.
Does not analyze gradual formation or removal of circuits, or whether a continuous progress measure anticipates a generalization jump.
Does not test grokking-like delays on non-algorithmic data or vary initialization scale or weight norm to induce a lazy-to-rich transition.
Does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test weight decay, circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
Does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts explain grokking delays.
